comments.text:
I live in Madison, that happened not very far at all from where we live. I watched multiple angles, multiple vids, very crystal clear audio... There was no justification for what they did. You could very clearly hear one of the cops run up and yell taser a few times, shoot and he very clearly reacted to it and was on the way down. There was NO reason at that point to suddenly react the way the one cop did. It's sad, because overall usually the police here have been doing a relatively alright job compared to a lot of places. Heat of the moment, high stress and the like, I get it, none of us have usually been in their shoes. But there's no reason to die for theft and having a knife and being a slight danger to the immediate vicinity but also being fairly held back. Criminal yes. Punished yes. Potentially injured in a struggle because you're lashing out and causing a problem yes. But unless he had a weapon that could threaten people farther away, the situation didn't justify the way they acted.

We absolutely should be pushing for more de-escalation and generally non-lethal attempts before it ever gets to this. There were so many options, even involving shooting, that could have ended better. There's no reason to execute, wounding can de-escalate a situation as well without doling out judgement without a trial. The guy was definitely a problem, but we need to push for better methods to handle these situations that don't end in an execution. They didn't even give the taser a chance, considering he fell to the ground and could very well have been controlled at that point.

That said, I don't believe the protesting is quite the right answer, but maybe it'll push politicians a bit more if we're lucky.
comments.author: @GlowstickRae
